standard.title: Select equipment and record data
standard.description: select and use equipment to generate and record data with precision, using digital tools as appropriate
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can follow safe procedures to investigate questions and use basic measurement tools (AC9S5I02). They have not yet selected equipment based on measurement range or precision requirements, or used digital tools to improve data quality.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students select and use appropriate equipment to generate and record data with precision, using digital tools as appropriate.

nodes.label: Selecting appropriate equipment
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can select equipment appropriate to an investigation's measurement needs and justify the choice
nodes.minimum_width: Select appropriate equipment for a given investigation; explain why the selected equipment suits the measurement task
nodes.typical_width: Select and use equipment appropriate to the investigation's measurement range; explain why a thermometer, measuring cylinder or force meter was chosen based on the expected measurement range
wider: Select equipment for an investigation where the expected measurement range is not given — estimate the range first, then choose
Compare two pieces of equipment for the same measurement task and justify which is more appropriate
Design a data collection system for a multi-variable investigation, justifying equipment selection

response_modes.reason: Students need to accumulate a repertoire of equipment types and their appropriate contexts — thermometers for temperature ranges, measuring cylinders for volumes, force meters for force ranges, digital sensors for abiotic factors — before they can make justified selection decisions in novel contexts. More equipment examples in varied investigation contexts build the selection vocabulary.

success_criteria: Selects equipment appropriate to the measurement task
Justifies the choice based on measurement range or precision
Does not select equipment that cannot measure the expected values

nodes.label: Recording data with precision
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can record data in organised formats using correct units and appropriate precision
nodes.minimum_width: Record data in a provided table using correct units; use appropriate precision for the equipment used
nodes.typical_width: Construct tables or spreadsheets to collect data; use standard units and perform simple unit conversions; record data to the precision of the equipment
wider: Limited width — recording data with correct units and consistent precision is a mechanical skill that does not vary across investigation contexts. Designing tables and evaluating recording errors are practice volume on the same conventions, not genuinely broader contexts.

response_modes.reason: Recording data with correct units and consistent precision is a mechanical skill where students commonly make careless errors — missing units, inconsistent decimal places, unlabelled columns. The skill does not vary across contexts; what helps is repeated practice with feedback on recording quality until correct habits are automatic.

success_criteria: Records data using correct standard units
Precision is appropriate to the equipment used
Data table is organised with clear headings and units

nodes.label: Using digital tools for data generation
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use digital tools to generate more precise or efficient data and explain the advantage over manual methods
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one digital tool that improves data precision or efficiency in a given investigation; explain the advantage
nodes.typical_width: Use digital tools such as sensors to measure abiotic factors and apps for field identification; compare precision of digital and analogue methods
wider: Evaluate how digital tools such as stopwatches and digital scales improve data precision compared to analogue equivalents
Use field identification apps that use image or call recognition during ecosystem investigations
Design a comparison between digital and manual data collection for the same investigation and analyse which produces more reliable data

response_modes.reason: Students need to encounter a range of digital tools — sensors, apps, spreadsheets, identification tools — across different investigation types to understand that 'digital tool' is a broad category with varied precision advantages. Each tool type adds a different dimension to the repertoire and prevents the overgeneralisation that digital is always more precise.

success_criteria: Identifies a digital tool appropriate for a given investigation
Explains the advantage of the digital tool over a manual alternative
Uses the tool to generate data with appropriate precision
